message.what: G3-G4 geomagnetic storm conditions are possible.
message.where: Worldwide and Earth's orbit. Higher-latitude regions face the greatest potential impacts.
message.when: There is a 70% chance that storm onset will occur between 1800 UTC Fri May 10 2024 and 0600 UTC Sat May 11 2024. Earliest Storm Onset: 1200 UTC Fri May 10 2024 Latest Storm Onset: 0600 UTC Sat May 11 2024
message.duration: Minimum Duration: 12 hours Maximum Duration: 48 hours
message.confidence: From 1200 UTC Fri May 10 2024 through 0600 UTC Mon May 13 2024, there is a 65% chance of G3 or greater conditions and a 20% chance of G4 or greater conditions.
message.impacts: Power systems may experience voltage-control issues, transformer stress, and isolated equipment trips. Atmospheric drag may lower satellite orbits and reduce the accuracy of tracking and orbit predictions. HF communication, precision satellite navigation, and some satellite communications may be intermittently degraded, particularly at higher latitudes. Geomagnetically induced currents may affect pipeline monitoring and corrosion-control systems. Aurora may be visible across much of the United States where darkness and local viewing conditions allow.
message.precautionary_preparedness_actions: Partners should review sector-specific procedures, monitor SWPC updates, and consult relevant decision-support guidance.
message.additional_details: Additional ensemble members indicate possible coronal mass ejection influences beyond the primary onset window. A Warning may be issued if G3 or greater conditions become expected.
message.next_update: No later than 2000 UTC Thu May 09 2024, or sooner if conditions change.
